channel.title: AI Security Paper Digest
channel.description: Curated papers on AI security from ArXiv and ACL

item.title: Auditing Black-Box LLM APIs with a Rank-Based Uniformity Test
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a rank-based uniformity statistical test to audit black-box LLM APIs for behavioral equality vs a locally held authentic model.
  • Targets provider-side tampering such as serving quantized models, harmful fine-tunes, response rerouting/mixing, and full model substitution.
  • Designed to be query-efficient and to avoid detectable query patterns, improving robustness against adversarial providers.
  • Evaluated under multiple threat scenarios including jailbreak prompts and model substitution, outperforming prior auditing methods under limited query budgets.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Xiaoyuan Zhu', 'Yaowen Ye', 'Tianyi Qiu', 'Hanlin Zhu', 'Sijun Tan', 'Ajraf Mannan', 'Jonathan Michala', 'Raluca Ada Popa', 'Willie Neiswanger']
  • Tags: ['LLM security auditing', 'Black-box model verification', 'Model substitution/quantization detection', 'Red teaming/robust evaluation']

item.title: Break Me If You Can: Self-Jailbreaking of Aligned LLMs via Lexical Insertion Prompting
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a new threat model: self-jailbreaking, where an aligned LLM can guide its own compromise without an external attacker model.
  • Introduces SLIP, a black-box breadth-first tree-search algorithm that incrementally inserts missing lexical content toward an attack goal using the target model as guidance.
  • Shows high jailbreak success (90–100% ASR, avg 94.7%) on AdvBench/HarmBench with relatively few LLM calls.
  • Evaluates defenses and proposes SDM (Semantic Drift Monitor) for detection, achieving 76% detection at 5% FPR but noting insufficiency vs adaptive attacks.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Devang Kulshreshtha', 'Hang Su', 'Haibo Jin', 'Chinmay Hegde', 'Haohan Wang']
  • Tags: ['jailbreaking', 'prompt injection', 'self-jailbreaking', 'attack-defense evaluation', 'LLM red teaming']

item.title: PIArena: A Platform for Prompt Injection Evaluation
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces PIArena, a unified, extensible platform to evaluate prompt injection attacks and corresponding defenses across multiple benchmarks.
  • Includes integration of state-of-the-art attacks and defenses and supports evaluation of robustness and cross-task generalization.
  • Proposes a dynamic, strategy-based adaptive attack that optimizes injected prompts using defense feedback.
  • Uses extensive experiments to identify limitations in current defenses, including poor generalization and susceptibility to adaptive attacks.

Paper Type

  • Research/Benchmarking

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Runpeng Geng', 'Chenlong Yin', 'Yanting Wang', 'Ying Chen', 'Jinyuan Jia']
  • Tags: ['prompt-injection', 'AI security evaluation', 'adversarial attacks', 'defense robustness']

item.title: Are GUI Agents Focused Enough? Automated Distraction via Semantic-level UI Element Injection
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a red-teaming threat model for GUI agents: Semantic-level UI Element Injection that overlays misleading, safety-aligned-looking UI elements onto screenshots to misdirect visual grounding.
  • Uses an Editor-Overlapper-Victim pipeline with iterative search to optimize overlay edits and adapt prompt strategies after failures.
  • Finds up to 4.4x improvement in attack success over random injection on strongest victims and demonstrates transferability across multiple victim models.
  • Shows the injected UI element can persistently attract the agent’s clicks in subsequent trials (>15% vs <1% for random injection).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Wenkui Yang', 'Chao Jin', 'Haisu Zhu', 'Weilin Luo', 'Derek Yuen', 'Kun Shao', 'Huaibo Huang', 'Junxian Duan', 'Jie Cao', 'Ran He']
  • Tags: ['GUI agents', 'red teaming', 'prompt-free UI element injection', 'adversarial attacks', 'visual grounding deception']

item.title: ACIArena: Toward Unified Evaluation for Agent Cascading Injection
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces ACIArena, a unified evaluation framework for Multi-Agent Systems under Agent Cascading Injection (ACI).
  • Defines systematic test suites across multiple attack surfaces (external inputs, agent profiles, inter-agent messages) and attack objectives (instruction hijacking, task disruption, information exfiltration).
  • Provides attack-defense evaluation modules, benchmarks 1,356 test cases across six MAS implementations, and analyzes limits of topology-only robustness and poor transfer of simplified defenses.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Hengyu An', 'Minxi Li', 'Jinghuai Zhang', 'Naen Xu', 'Chunyi Zhou', 'Changjiang Li', 'Xiaogang Xu', 'Tianyu Du', 'Shouling Ji']
  • Tags: ['multi-agent security', 'agent cascading injection', 'robustness evaluation/benchmark', 'attack surfaces and objectives', 'attack-defense benchmarking']

item.title: The Art of (Mis)alignment: How Fine-Tuning Methods Effectively Misalign and Realign LLMs in Post-Training
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies how various LLM fine-tuning methods can be used to effectively induce misalignment and then restore alignment (realignment).
  • Evaluates multiple supervised and preference fine-tuning approaches (e.g., ORPO for misalignment, DPO for realignment) on safety-aligned base models.
  • Finds an asymmetry between attack (misalignment) and defense (realignment), including model-specific resistance and residual multi-round adversarial effects.
  • Emphasizes the need for robust safeguards and tailored safety-alignment strategies before deploying third-party LLMs.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Rui Zhang', 'Hongwei Li', 'Yun Shen', 'Xinyue Shen', 'Wenbo Jiang', 'Guowen Xu', 'Yang Liu', 'Michael Backes', 'Yang Zhang']
  • Tags: ['LLM security', 'misalignment attacks via fine-tuning', 'alignment/realignment', 'post-training manipulation']

item.title: IatroBench: Pre-Registered Evidence of Iatrogenic Harm from AI Safety Measures
item.description:
Summary

  • Introduces IatroBench, a pre-registered benchmark evaluating iatrogenic harm from AI safety measures in medication/tapering clinical scenarios.
  • Tests multiple frontier LLMs on physician vs layperson framing to quantify commission harm (unsafe actions given) and omission harm (withholding needed guidance).
  • Finds identity-contingent withholding: models give better (less omission harm) guidance to physician-framed prompts than layperson-framed equivalents, with the widest gap for the most heavily safety-invested model.
  • Identifies distinct failure modes (trained withholding, incompetence, and token-density-based content filtering) and shows evaluator/judge blind spots in omission-harm scoring.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking/Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['David Gringras']
  • Tags: ['AI safety evaluation', 'Jailbreak/identity-contingent prompting effects', 'Safety guardrail failure modes', 'Medical/clinical harm benchmarking', 'LLM red teaming benchmark']

item.title: Guardian-as-an-Advisor: Advancing Next-Generation Guardian Models for Trustworthy LLMs
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes a “Guardian-as-an-Advisor” soft-gating safety pipeline for LLMs that predicts a risk label and explanation, then prepends advice to the user query for re-inference while keeping the base model within its original spec.
  • Introduces GuardSet, a 208k+ multi-domain dataset unifying harmful/harmless cases and including robustness and honesty slices for training/evaluating the guard.
  • Trains GuardAdvisor with SFT and then RL to enforce consistency between predicted labels and explanations; evaluates advisory-augmented responses improving helpfulness versus unaugmented prompts.
  • Reports low overhead (advisor <5% of base compute; 2–10% end-to-end latency under harmful-input rates).

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Yue Huang', 'Haomin Zhuang', 'Jiayi Ye', 'Han Bao', 'Yanbo Wang', 'Hang Hua', 'Siyuan Wu', 'Pin-Yu Chen', 'Xiangliang Zhang']
  • Tags: ['LLM safety', 'Guardrails', 'Attack detection/robustness', 'Honesty/robustness evaluation']

item.title: How Independent are Large Language Models? A Statistical Framework for Auditing Behavioral Entanglement and Reweighting Verifier Ensembles
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes an auditing framework to measure behavioral entanglement (dependency) among black-box LLMs using information-theoretic metrics.
  • Analyzes how entanglement affects multi-model evaluation, especially LLM-as-a-judge pipelines, showing entanglement correlates with judge over-endorsement/precision degradation.
  • Demonstrates a defense-like application by reweighting verifier ensembles to reduce correlated bias, improving verification accuracy over majority voting.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Chenchen Kuai', 'Jiwan Jiang', 'Zihao Zhu', 'Hao Wang', 'Keshu Wu', 'Zihao Li', 'Yunlong Zhang', 'Chenxi Liu', 'Zhengzhong Tu', 'Zhiwen Fan', 'Yang Zhou']
  • Tags: ['LLM security evaluation', 'Ensemble robustness', 'Model dependency/entanglement', 'Evaluation bias mitigation', 'Information-theoretic auditing']

item.title: AtomEval: Atomic Evaluation of Adversarial Claims in Fact Verification
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes AtomEval to evaluate adversarial claim rewrites for fact verification using truth-conditional consistency rather than surface similarity.
  • Introduces Atomic Validity Scoring (AVS) by decomposing claims into subject-relation-object-modifier (SROM) atoms to detect factual corruption.
  • Experiments on FEVER evaluate adversarial rewrite strategies and LLM-based adversarial generators, showing improved reliability of evaluation signals and limitations of current adversarial evaluation practices.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Hongyi Cen', 'Mingxin Wang', 'Yule Liu', 'Jingyi Zheng', 'Hanze Jia', 'Tan Tang', 'Yingcai Wu']
  • Tags: ['adversarial evaluation', 'fact verification', 'adversarial claim rewriting', 'LLM robustness', 'benchmark/metrics']

item.title: An Empirical Analysis of Static Analysis Methods for Detection and Mitigation of Code Library Hallucinations
item.description:
Summary

  • Studies whether static analysis tools can detect and mitigate LLM code library hallucinations (non-existent APIs/features).
  • Empirically evaluates detection rates for general code errors and specifically library hallucinations across LLMs and datasets.
  • Characterizes limitations via manual analysis, providing upper bounds on what static methods can catch.
  • Concludes static analysis is a relatively cheap mitigation approach but cannot fully eliminate hallucinations.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Clarissa Miranda-Pena', 'Andrew Reeson', "C\\'ecile Paris", 'Josiah Poon', 'Jonathan K. Kummerfeld']
  • Tags: ['AI safety', 'Code hallucinations', 'Static analysis', 'Vulnerability detection/mitigation']

item.title: Beyond Social Pressure: Benchmarking Epistemic Attack in Large Language Models
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes PPT-Bench to benchmark “epistemic attack” on LLMs via prompts that challenge knowledge, values, or identity.
  • Defines a Philosophical Pressure Taxonomy with four attack types: Epistemic Destabilization, Value Nullification, Authority Inversion, and Identity Dissolution.
  • Evaluates responses at three interaction layers (baseline, single-turn pressure, and multi-turn Socratic escalation) to measure inconsistency and conversational capitulation.
  • Tests multiple mitigation approaches, showing results vary by attack type and model, with best-performing interventions differing for API vs open models.

Paper Type

  • Benchmarking/Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Steven Au', 'Sujit Noronha']
  • Tags: ['epistemic attacks', 'LLM safety evaluation', 'benchmarking', 'mitigation/defense']

item.title: ADAG: Automatically Describing Attribution Graphs
item.description:
Summary

  • Proposes ADAG, an automated pipeline to generate natural-language descriptions of attribution/circuit-tracing graphs for interpretability.
  • Uses attribution profiles (input/output gradient effects) plus feature clustering to group circuit components by functional role.
  • Employs an LLM explainer–simulator setup to generate and score explanations for feature groups.
  • Demonstrates ADAG on circuit-tracing benchmarks and applies it to identify steerable clusters responsible for a harmful advice jailbreak in Llama 3.1 8B Instruct.

Paper Type

  • Research

Additional Information

  • Authors: ['Aryaman Arora', 'Zhengxuan Wu', 'Jacob Steinhardt', 'Sarah Schwettmann']
  • Tags: ['model interpretability', 'circuit tracing', 'jailbreaking', 'LLM explainability']
